title: Rerank endpoint p99 tail reduction and tenant-aware ingress shaping
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The rerank endpoint is increasingly used by customers for high-quality candidate ordering (cross-encoder style reranking). Unlike single-embedding lookups, rerank has a high variance in CPU/GPU work per request (K candidates, model variant, sequence lengths), which manifests as pronounced p99 tail latency and burst-induced 503/504 behavior when queues back up. Several customers running synchronous search UXes have reported p99 latencies in the 300-800ms range during bursts, causing poor UX and retries that exacerbate load.

Goal: Reduce observable p99 tail latency by 2.5x for typical tenant traffic while preserving throughput and predictable cost. Introduce tenant-aware ingress shaping + admission control so heavy tenants cannot cause global tail events. Provide a safe rollout path that can be toggled per-tenant and monitored.

Key constraints and assumptions:
- We must maintain API compatibility: same request/response schema for rerank (no client changes).
- Some customers run large-K reranks (K>64) and/or longer sequences; these are expected to remain relatively heavy.
- GPU allocation exhaustion must not cascade to other endpoints (embeddings/generation).

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Fast-path vs heavy-path split: detect requests that are eligible for a fast-path rerank (short sequences, K<=16, model variants marked as "fast-rank") and route them to a low-latency pool optimized for small-batch, low-lag execution (CPU+quantized GPU variants). Heavy-path requests route to a separate GPU pool with batching optimized for throughput.

2) Tenant-aware ingress shaping: maintain per-tenant leaky-bucket token buckets that rate-limit admitted concurrency into each pool. Admission decisions use a sliding window of recent success latency and queue length to dynamically reduce admission for tenants contributing to tail spikes.

3) Priority-aware admission and partial results: when heavy-path queues exceed thresholds, return a deterministic partial result (top-N from fast-pass) + background continuation to compute final score; clients can optionally poll or receive webhook when final ranking is ready. This trades synchronous latency for eventual correctness for heavy requests and reduces burst amplification from client retries.

4) Backpressure semantics and Retry-After: unify HTTP 429/503 semantics for rerank ingress with clear Retry-After headers and client hints to reduce immediate retries. Document recommended client-side backoff in SDK.

5) Autoscaler changes: add a short-window reactive autoscaler tuned for rerank pools that reacts to queue depth + p95 latency increase (not only CPU/GPU util) to provision warm capacity faster. Combine with proactive warm-pools seeded by predictive signals from query trace forecasting.

6) Synthetic calibration and chaos tests: run nightly synthetic replay of sampled prod traces to validate admission policies and ensure no tenant can cause cross-tenant SLA violation. Introduce simulated noise to validate p99 resilience.

Trade-offs considered:
- Overprovisioning fast-path pool reduces p99 but increases GPU-hours; we mitigate via predictive warm-pool and smaller fast-quantized models.
- Returning partial results impacts accuracy for some customers; this is gated behind tenant opt-in and for large-K only.
- Introducing webhooks/polling increases client complexity; we will provide SDK helpers to abstract polling and graceful degradation.

Design artifacts and links:
- Initial perf analysis notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/rerank-p99-analysis-2026-02
- Architecture diagram and flow: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RERANK/Rerank+ingress+shaping+design
- Proposed schema changes for response partial flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/specs/pull/48 (draft)

Metrics and success criteria (see acceptance_criteria below). Cost model: initial estimate +7%-12% GPU-hours for fast-path capacity but projected net reduction in cost per useful query because retries and error rates fall.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): internal tenants + 3 low-volume customers (feature flag) - 1 week
- Stage 2 (regional ramp): enable ingress shaping for non-enterprise tenants in us-east-1 with monitoring thresholds and auto rollback - 2 weeks
- Stage 3 (enterprise opt-in): offer partial-results behavior as opt-in for enterprise tenants with an SDK helper - ongoing

Monitoring and alerts:
- New dashboards: rerank-p95/p99 by tenant, queue depth by pool, admission drop-rate by tenant, 429/503 rate by endpoint.
- Alert if p99 > 250ms for >5min for any production tenant or if global 429 rate > 0.5% sustained.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1: Fast-path detection + routing (instrumentation + feature flag)
- M2: Per-tenant admission controller and token buckets + metrics
- M3: Priority admission + partial-results path + SDK helpers
- M4: Reactive autoscaler + predictive warm-pools
- M5: Calibration harness and chaos tests

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for admission controller logic and buckets
- Load tests using recorded traces with k-variations and sequence-length sweeps
- End-to-end canary on staging with mirrored traffic for 48h before prod canary

Documentation and SDK changes:
- SDK: backoff helpers and polling helpers, exposed as a single-line opt-in
- Console: per-tenant rerank dashboard and admit/drop explanation UI

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Miscalibrated token buckets throttle healthy tenants. Mitigation: conservative defaults + monitoring + immediate rollback flag.
- Risk: Partial-results UX could be confusing. Mitigation: clear response field "partial": true and SDK gracefully surfaces.
- Risk: Increased cost for fast-path pool. Mitigation: quantized models and usage-based billing to customers; measure ROI by reduced retries.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for rerank (global baseline traffic mix) reduced by >= 2x compared to baseline (baseline measured 2026-02-10)
p99 latency reduced to <= 250ms for fast-path eligible traffic and <= 500ms for heavy-path traffic under typical load
No cascading failures: unrelated endpoints (embeddings/generation) show no increase in 5xx errors during canary
Per-tenant admission prevents any single tenant from contributing >30% of global rerank p99 budget during burst tests
Automated synthetic replay runs show <1% increase in error rate vs baseline and p99 targets met in 90% of runs
Feature-flagged rollout completed to initial canary tenants with monitored rollback thresholds and runbook documented
